lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: verifying inverse relationships by composition

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: Why does sine on all real numbers not have an inverse function without further restriction?
choices: It repeats with period π, so the domain is restricted to (−π/2, π/2) to make an inverse possible.
Because its outputs are not all positive.
It is not one-to-one, so the domain is restricted to [0, π] to make an inverse possible.
It is not one-to-one — infinitely many inputs give the same output — so it has no inverse until the domain is restricted to [−π/2, π/2].

items.prompt: Find all solutions of sin θ = 1/2 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Evaluate arcsin(√2/2) in radians, giving the principal value.
Why does cosine on all real numbers not have an inverse function without further restriction?
choices: It repeats with period π, so the domain is restricted to (−π/2, π/2) to make an inverse possible.
Because its outputs are not all positive.
It is not one-to-one — infinitely many inputs give the same output — so it has no inverse until the domain is restricted to [−π/2, π/2].
It is not one-to-one, so the domain is restricted to [0, π] to make an inverse possible.

items.prompt: Find all solutions of sin θ = √2/2 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°.
Evaluate arcsin(0) in radians, giving the principal value.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: Why does tangent on all real numbers where it is defined not have an inverse function without further restriction?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Find all solutions of sin θ = √3/2 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
